passages.text: Every high priest is appointed from among men to represent them in matters relating to God, to offer gifts and sacrifices for sins.
passages.sermon:
A high priest is a man chosen from among people.
God appoints the high priest to represent people before Him.
The high priest offers gifts to God for the people.
The high priest also offers sacrifices to God for the sins of the people.
passages.original: Πᾶς γὰρ ἀρχιερεὺς ἐξ ἀνθρώπων λαμβανόμενος ὑπὲρ ἀνθρώπων καθίσταται τὰ πρὸς τὸν Θεόν ἵνα προσφέρῃ δῶρά τε καὶ θυσίας ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτιῶν

passages.text: He is able to deal gently with those who are ignorant and misguided, since he himself is beset by weakness.
passages.sermon:
A high priest comes from among men.
He represents people before God.
He offers gifts and sacrifices for sins.
He can deal gently with those who are ignorant.
He can deal gently with those who are misguided.
He does this because he himself has weakness.
passages.original: μετριοπαθεῖν δυνάμενος τοῖς ἀγνοοῦσιν καὶ πλανωμένοις ἐπεὶ καὶ αὐτὸς περίκειται ἀσθένειαν

passages.text: That is why he is obligated to offer sacrifices for his own sins, as well as for the sins of the people.
passages.sermon:
The high priest is a man chosen from among men.
He represents people before God.
He offers gifts and sacrifices for sins.
He is weak, just like the people.
Because of his weakness, he must offer sacrifices for his own sins.
He must also offer sacrifices for the sins of the people.
passages.original: καὶ δι’ αὐτὴν ὀφείλει καθὼς περὶ τοῦ λαοῦ οὕτως καὶ περὶ αὑτοῦ προσφέρειν περὶ ἁμαρτιῶν

passages.text: No one takes this honor upon himself; he must be called by God, just as Aaron was.
passages.sermon:
A person cannot take this honor for himself.
God must call him to this honor.
God called Aaron in this way.
Aaron did not choose this honor for himself.
God chose Aaron.
passages.original: Καὶ οὐχ ἑαυτῷ τις λαμβάνει τὴν τιμήν ἀλλὰ καλούμενος ὑπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ καθώσπερ καὶ Ἀαρών

passages.text: So also Christ did not take upon Himself the glory of becoming a high priest, but He was called by the One who said to Him: “You are My Son; today I have become Your Father.”
passages.sermon:
Christ is the Son of God.
Christ did not give Himself the honor of becoming high priest.
God called Christ to be high priest.
God spoke to Christ.
God said, “You are My Son.”
God said, “Today I have become Your Father.”
passages.original: Οὕτως καὶ ὁ Χριστὸς οὐχ ἑαυτὸν ἐδόξασεν γενηθῆναι ἀρχιερέα ἀλλ’ ὁ λαλήσας πρὸς αὐτόν Υἱός μου εἶ σύ ἐγὼ σήμερον γεγέννηκά σε

passages.text: And in another passage God says: “You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.”
passages.sermon: God speaks in another passage.\r\nGod says, “You are a priest forever.”\r\nGod says, “You are a priest in the order of Melchizedek.”
passages.original: Καθὼς καὶ ἐν ἑτέρῳ λέγει Σὺ ἱερεὺς εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισέδεκ

passages.text: During the days of Jesus’ earthly life, He offered up prayers and petitions with loud cries and tears to the One who could save Him from death, and He was heard because of His reverence.
passages.sermon:
Jesus lived on earth as a man.
During His life on earth, Jesus prayed.
He brought prayers and requests to God.
God had the power to save Jesus from death.
Jesus prayed with loud cries.
Jesus prayed with tears.
God heard Jesus.
God listened to Jesus because Jesus showed deep reverence.
passages.original: Ὃς ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις τῆς σαρκὸς αὐτοῦ δεήσεις τε καὶ ἱκετηρίας πρὸς τὸν δυνάμενον σῴζειν αὐτὸν ἐκ θανάτου μετὰ κραυγῆς ἰσχυρᾶς καὶ δακρύων προσενέγκας καὶ εἰσακουσθεὶς ἀπὸ τῆς εὐλαβείας

passages.text: Although He was a Son, He learned obedience from what He suffered.
passages.sermon: Jesus is the Son of God.\r\nHe suffered many things.\r\nHe learned obedience through what He suffered.
passages.original: καίπερ ὢν Υἱός ἔμαθεν ἀφ’ ὧν ἔπαθεν τὴν ὑπακοήν

passages.text: And having been made perfect, He became the source of eternal salvation to all who obey Him and was designated by God as high priest in the order of Melchizedek.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
God made Jesus perfect.
God appointed Jesus as high priest.
God made Jesus high priest in the order of Melchizedek.
Jesus became the source of eternal salvation.
Jesus gives eternal salvation to all who obey Him.
passages.original: καὶ τελειωθεὶς ἐγένετο πᾶσιν τοῖς ὑπακούουσιν αὐτῷ αἴτιος σωτηρίας αἰωνίου προσαγορευθεὶς ὑπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀρχιερεὺς κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισέδεκ

passages.text: We have much to say about this, but it is hard to explain, because you are dull of hearing.
passages.sermon:
We have much to say about this.
This subject is important.
This subject is deep.
It is hard to explain these things.
You have become slow to listen.
Your understanding is dull.
This makes it difficult to teach you.
passages.original: Περὶ οὗ πολὺς ἡμῖν ὁ λόγος καὶ δυσερμήνευτος λέγειν ἐπεὶ νωθροὶ γεγόνατε ταῖς ἀκοαῖς

passages.text: Although by this time you ought to be teachers, you need someone to reteach you the basic principles of God’s word. You need milk, not solid food!
passages.sermon:
You have followed Christ for a long time.
You should be teachers by now.
But you still need someone to teach you.
You need to learn the basic principles of God’s word again.
You are not ready for deeper teaching.
You need milk.
You do not need solid food.
passages.original: καὶ γὰρ ὀφείλοντες εἶναι διδάσκαλοι διὰ τὸν χρόνον πάλιν χρείαν ἔχετε τοῦ διδάσκειν ὑμᾶς τινα τὰ στοιχεῖα τῆς ἀρχῆς τῶν λογίων τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ γεγόνατε χρείαν ἔχοντες γάλακτος καὶ οὐ στερεᾶς τροφῆς

passages.text: For everyone who lives on milk is still an infant, inexperienced in the message of righteousness.
passages.sermon: Everyone who lives on milk is an infant.\r\nAn infant is inexperienced in the message of righteousness.
passages.original: πᾶς γὰρ ὁ μετέχων γάλακτος ἄπειρος λόγου δικαιοσύνης νήπιος γάρ ἐστιν

passages.text: But solid food is for the mature, who by constant use have trained their senses to distinguish good from evil.
passages.sermon: Solid food is for mature people.\r\nMature people have trained their senses by constant use.\r\nThey can distinguish good from evil.
passages.original: τελείων δέ ἐστιν ἡ στερεὰ τροφή τῶν διὰ τὴν ἕξιν τὰ αἰσθητήρια γεγυμνασμένα ἐχόντων πρὸς διάκρισιν καλοῦ τε καὶ κακοῦ
